gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how many late-night sessions each quiet pick lasts on one charge. At a stated 2 hours a night, the EasySMX X05 Pro lasts 3 nights (HLPLANET: about 6 h), the standard Mobapad Chitu 2 about 7 (HLPLANET: about 15 h) and the GameSir Super Nova 9 (Wccftech: 18 h).
standout_why: Compared against the cited rivals I could open or check: our own page (dealectric.com, cited), the manuals.plus Super Nova manual (cited) and the HLPLANET G7 page (cited). I could not read the cited Reddit threads: reddit.com blocked fetching. Our page gives runtimes in hours (X05 Pro 6 to 9 h, standard Chitu 2 15 h) but no runtime for the Super Nova and no per-night figure. A search summary says the manuals.plus manual lists about 15 h for the Super Nova, but I could not read the PDF itself, so treat that as possible overlap. No rival page turns hours into nights between charges at a stated session length, and none says that the most-recommended quiet pad has the shortest runtime of the quiet group.
decides: This confirms the X05 Pro as the quietest-for-the-money pick, but with a cost the page should state. Its measured runtime is the shortest of the quiet candidates: 3 nights at 2 h, against 9 for the Super Nova. A shopper who plays wireless at night and doesn't want to charge every few days should look at the Super Nova (it ships with a charging dock) or the Chitu 2. Wired or 2.4 GHz-dongle play near the PC makes this moot. Separately, EasySMX's own X05 Pro page describes the D-pad as 'tactile microswitch'. That contradicts ChatGPT's 'silicone-damped D-pad' line, so the page should say only the face buttons are maker-confirmed as silicone-damped.
